info.name: Bejo API
info.description: Select a Postman environment before sending requests — import bejo.local.postman_environment.json (Bejo — Local) or bejo.production.postman_environment.json (Bejo — Production). Each defines baseUrl, apiToken, and token. The Login request auto-saves the JWT into the active environment's `token`.

request.description:
Self-service registration. Creates a NEW BUSINESS and its first user as the SUPER_ADMIN (SELF_SERVICE) + bank profile. No JWT required — only X-API-TOKEN. No QRIS row is created (QRIS is optional; add one later via /api/qris/upload).

Mandatory: username, password, name, email, phone, businessName.
Optional: businessAddress, nmid, bankName, bankNumber, bankAccountName.

Returns HTTP 201 on success.
List the users of the caller's business (any member). The SUPER_ADMIN (creator) is first.

Add a user to the caller's business as a MEMBER. Only the SUPER_ADMIN may do this (else 403). Rejected (400) if the username is taken or the business is at its user cap (BUSINESS_MAX_USERS, default 5, incl. the super admin).

Returns HTTP 201 on success.
Partial update of a member (name/email/phone/password; all optional). Super admin only (403 otherwise). A super admin cannot be modified here (403).
Soft-delete a member (releases its username for reuse; removes its sessions). Super admin only (403). A super admin cannot be deleted (403).

Authenticate with username + password. The test script auto-saves the JWT to `{{token}}`.

Response `data` includes: id, username, accountType, name, email, isEmailVerified, phone, isPhoneVerified, businessRole (SUPER_ADMIN|MEMBER), businessName, businessAddress, nmid, bankName, bankNumber, bankAccountName, profilePicture (business picture, null when unset), appSettings (bundled), token, tokenType, expiresIn.

The bundled profilePicture + appSettings save the client extra round trips on the home screen; GET /api/users/me returns the same bundle minus the token.

Invalidates the current JWT — it cannot be used again after logout. Optional body { deviceId } also clears that device's stored FCM token (the user's other devices are untouched); omit the body to just blacklist the token. The test script clears {{token}} from the collection variables.

query.description: Filter start date (inclusive), format: yyyy-MM-dd. Optional.
Filter end date (inclusive), format: yyyy-MM-dd. Optional.

request.description:
Returns transaction history for the authenticated user, ordered by date descending.

Each transaction includes: transactionId, transactionDate, amount (integer), type (MANAGED/MANUAL/PARSED), acquirer, issuerName, merchantName, merchantPan (optional), customerPan (optional), rrn (optional).

Optional date filter: dateStart and/or dateEnd (format yyyy-MM-dd, both inclusive).

Paginated: optional page (default 1) + size (default 50, max 200). The response adds page, totalPages, and total; count is the number of items in the current page.

query.description: The client's local today (yyyy-MM-dd). Optional; drives the today/yesterday/month buckets. Defaults to the server date.

request.description:
Dashboard totals: summed amount + count for today, yesterday, and the current calendar month. Use this instead of summing the (now paginated) history.

Response data: { date, today: {totalAmount, count}, yesterday: {...}, month: {...} }. Empty ranges return zeros. Pass ?date= to align the buckets with the merchant's timezone.

header.description: UUID per request attempt. Sending the same key again returns the existing transactionId without inserting a duplicate.

request.description:
Manually records a transaction. The server generates transactionId.

Idempotency-Key header is required — use a UUID per request attempt. Resubmitting the same key returns the same transactionId without inserting a duplicate.

For MANUAL type, acquirer is automatically set to 'Cash'.
Mandatory: type, transactionDate, amount.
Optional: issuerName, merchantPan, customerPan, rrn.

Returns HTTP 201 with { transactionId }.

header.description: UUID per request attempt. Sending the same key again returns the existing transactionId without inserting a duplicate.

request.description:
Records a transaction from an external acquirer. The server generates transactionId.

Idempotency-Key header is required. For PARSED type, acquirer is required.

Returns HTTP 201 with { transactionId }.

Bulk-create manually-entered transactions synced after offline entry. Each item has its own idempotencyKey (client-generated) so re-sending the batch never duplicates. Partial success: one bad item does not block the rest.

Returns HTTP 200 with a summary (total/created/duplicate/failed) and a per-item results list; match each result back by idempotencyKey. Item status is CREATED, DUPLICATE (already synced), or FAILED (with error). Batch limits: 1–500 items.

variable.description: transactionId returned by Add Transaction / history

request.description:
Edits the authenticated user's transaction. Partial update — only fields present in the body are changed; type cannot be changed. Only MANUAL/PARSED transactions can be edited — MANAGED ones are immutable.

Optional fields (send at least one): transactionDate, amount, acquirer, issuerName, merchantPan, customerPan, rrn, items.

items = FULL REPLACEMENT of the sold-product line items (array of { productId, quantity }). It reconciles stock by the per-product delta vs. the existing items (increased/added lines draw more stock — validated; reduced/removed lines return stock), records one SALE stock mutation, and (for a non-empty list) re-derives amount from the subtotals. An empty list [] clears all items and returns their stock; omitting items leaves them unchanged. The response includes the post-edit items.

Returns HTTP 200 with the updated transaction.
Errors: 400 (no fields / MANAGED type / invalid amount / blank acquirer / insufficient stock / unknown or duplicate product), 404 Transaction not found (unknown, deleted, or another user's transaction).

variable.description: transactionId returned by Add Transaction / history

request.description:
Soft-deletes the authenticated user's transaction: the row keeps a deleted_at timestamp and disappears from history. Cannot be undone via the API.

If the transaction has sold-product line items, deleting it RETURNS each item's quantity to its product's stock and records a SALE reversal stock mutation (a product deleted since the sale is skipped). The line-item records are kept; stock is returned exactly once.

Returns HTTP 200.
Errors: 404 Transaction not found (unknown, already deleted, or another user's transaction).

request.description:
TEST endpoint — sends an FCM push notification (built from this payload) to the specified device. Does NOT record any transaction.

data.transactionId, data.transactionDate, data.amount, and data.issuerName are required. merchantPan, customerPan, and rrn are optional.

Requires Firebase to be configured (503 if not). Real payments are recorded and pushed by the QRIS Callback (QR MPM Notify).

TEST/UTILITY — broadcasts an FCM push to ALL of the caller's devices at once (no deviceId). Best-effort: a dead token never fails the call (and is auto-cleaned); zero devices still returns 200. Does NOT record a transaction. Same body as Send Test Notification but without deviceId.

Requires Firebase to be configured (503 if not).
Updates the FCM push token for a device. Replace `device-001` in the path with the actual device ID.

Returns the caller's own account bundle: id, profile, businessRole, and the shared business/bank/profilePicture/appSettings — the same shape as the login data minus the token fields. Use it to refresh state without re-logging-in, and to get your own id for identifying yourself in the members list.

Updates name, email, and phone. All three fields are required.

Phone must be in international format, e.g. +628123456789.

Updates the business name, address, and NMID (shared by all of the business's users). businessName is required; businessAddress and nmid are optional.

Does NOT change the initial (regulatory) values. Use Reset Business Info to revert.

Reverts businessName, businessAddress, and nmid to the values recorded at registration.

No request body needed.

Updates bank account information (shared by all of the business's users). All three fields are required.

bankNumber must be digits only, 6–20 digits.

Does NOT change the initial (regulatory) values. Use Reset Bank Info to revert.

Reverts bankName, bankNumber, and bankAccountName to the values recorded at registration (initialBankName / initialBankNumber / initialBankAccountName).

No request body needed.

Changes the authenticated user's password. Requires the current password for verification.

newPassword rules: minimum 8 characters, at least 1 letter and 1 number.
Returns the BUSINESS picture as a base64 string (shared by all of the business's users). Optional — when unset, data.profilePicture is explicitly null (no placeholder).

Stores a base64-encoded image as the BUSINESS picture (shared by all members). Compress client-side; the decoded image must be <= 1 MB. Returns the saved picture. NOTE: super admin only — a plain member gets 403.
Clears the BUSINESS picture (sets it back to null). Idempotent — succeeds whether or not a picture was set. NOTE: super admin only — a plain member gets 403.
Creates a product category (unique name per merchant). Returns HTTP 201 with { id, name, createdAt }.
Lists the merchant's product categories.
Deletes a category. Its products are un-categorized (categoryId -> null), not deleted. Replace 1 with the category id.

Creates a product (SKU). sku + name required; sku unique per merchant. categoryId (optional) must be one of the merchant's own categories. photo (optional) is a base64 image, max 500 KB decoded. Returns HTTP 201 with the product incl. resolved categoryName.

Lists the merchant's products. Optional ?categoryId= filter. The photo field is omitted from list items to keep the payload small — use Get Product for the image.

Paginated: optional page (default 1) + size (default 50, max 200). The response adds page, totalPages, and total; count is the number of items in the current page.
Returns one product including its photo. Replace 1 with the product id.
Partial update: send any subset of sku, name, categoryId, price, costPrice, stock, photo. Managing inventory = send { "stock": N }. Replace 1 with the product id.
Hard-deletes a product. Replace 1 with the product id.

Stock opname: sets several products' stock to their newly counted quantities at once. Each item's stock is the new absolute count. Optional note is stored on the resulting ADJUSTMENT stock mutation. Atomic — if any productId isn't the merchant's, the whole adjustment is rejected. Returns a variance report (previousStock/newStock/difference) per product.

Records a PURCHASE (restock) stock mutation: raises the stock of every listed product at once and saves line items with before/after stock. Atomic — if any productId isn't the merchant's, the whole thing is rejected. unitPrice defaults to the product's costPrice when omitted. Returns HTTP 201 with type=PURCHASE, totalAmount + item snapshots.

Stock-change history newest-first — mutations (PURCHASE from restock, ADJUSTMENT from stock opname, UPDATE from a product edit that changed stock), each with its line items.

Paginated: optional page (default 1) + size (default 50, max 200). The response adds page, totalPages, and total; count is the number of items in the current page.
Returns one stock mutation including its line items (previousStock/newStock/quantityChange). Replace 1 with the mutation id.

item.name: Presence

request.description:
Employee clock-in. MEMBER only — a super admin gets 403 (they don't take attendance).

latitude, longitude and clockDatetime are required; note is optional (max 255). clockDatetime is the device's local (WIB) time, so an entry made offline keeps its real time when it syncs — but more than a day in the future is rejected (400).

ONCE PER DAY: a member may clock in at most once per calendar day. A repeat is rejected with 400 "Kamu sudah absen masuk hari ini"; the next day resets. (A clock-out on the same day is still allowed — the limit is one of each type.)

Pushes a display notification to the business's super admin: "<username> telah absen masuk!" / "Pastikan jadwal absen sesuai prosedur. Sukses terus ya!". Returns 201 with the recorded entry (type=CLOCK_IN).

Employee clock-out — same body as clock-in, records type=CLOCK_OUT and pushes "<username> telah absen keluar!" to the super admin.

Also limited to once per calendar day (400 "Kamu sudah absen keluar hari ini" on a repeat).

Requires that day's clock-in (400 "Kamu belum absen masuk hari ini") — you can't leave a shift you never started. A shift never spans midnight: a clock-out at 01:00 belongs to the new day and needs a clock-in on it.

Super-admin spot-check to the WHOLE TEAM — omit userId (send an empty body). Records one PING entry per MEMBER of the business.

Only members are pinged — never the super admin's own devices.

Pushes each targeted member a data-only, high-priority push: title "Ping Absen Bejoo!", body "Halo Mas/Mbak Bejo Sekalian. Masih pada Semangaat?" (fixed copy).

The ping carries no note — the note on a PING entry is reserved for the MEMBER's reply, sent with POST /api/presences/{id}/respond.

403 for a plain member, 400 if the business has no members yet.

COOLDOWN: a member can only be pinged once an HOUR. A targeted ping inside that hour is rejected with 400 ("... baru saja di-ping. Coba lagi dalam N menit"). On a team-wide ping, members pinged within the hour are SKIPPED and the rest are pinged — the response's count/data shows who actually got it; 400 only if every member is still cooling down.

Only members that can actually receive it are pinged: a member with NO REGISTERED DEVICE is left out (writing a PING for them would burn their hour-long cooldown on a message nothing could deliver), as is one pinged within the last hour.

The response reports how many of the team were reached — data.pinged / data.totalMembers, plus data.skipped[] (each with reason NO_DEVICE or COOLDOWN) and data.presences[] (the entries created). No message is composed server-side; the app builds its own sentence from the counts.

Same endpoint, but userId targets ONE member instead of the whole team. Get the id from GET /api/users/members.

Pushes each targeted member a data-only, high-priority push: title "Ping Absen Bejoo!", body "Halo Mas/Mbak Bejo Sekalian. Masih pada Semangaat?" (fixed copy).

The ping carries no note — the note on a PING entry is reserved for the MEMBER's reply, sent with POST /api/presences/{id}/respond.

400 if userId isn't an active member of your own business (an unknown id, another business's staff, or your own super-admin id) — nothing is sent.

COOLDOWN: a member can only be pinged once an HOUR. A targeted ping inside that hour is rejected with 400 ("... baru saja di-ping. Coba lagi dalam N menit"). On a team-wide ping, members pinged within the hour are SKIPPED and the rest are pinged — the response's count/data shows who actually got it; 400 only if every member is still cooling down.

A targeted ping to a member with no registered device, or one pinged within the last hour, is rejected with 400 — you asked for that person by name, so you're told it didn't happen.

variable.description: The PING entry's id (from the ping response or the presence list).

request.description:
The member taps the ping in the app and replies WITH THEIR LOCATION. Stamps responseDatetime on their own PING entry, exactly once (a conditional update, so two simultaneous taps can't both stamp it).

latitude + longitude are REQUIRED — a ping is a spot-check, so the answer must say where the member actually is. note is optional.

A PING entry is created with no location and no note; this is the only thing that writes them. The super admin reads the reply (response time + coordinates + note) in the presence history.

403 if the ping belongs to another user; 400 if the location is missing, the entry isn't a PING, or it was already responded to; 404 if it isn't in the caller's business.

WITHIN 24 HOURS: a ping expires 24 hours after it was sent (400 "sudah kedaluwarsa"). A rolling window, not a calendar date — a ping sent at 23:00 stays answerable through the night. ONCE ONLY: the member may have several devices, but only the first reply is accepted — a second gets 400 "Ping ini sudah direspons".

query.description: Filter to one team member. Super admin only — a member passing someone else's id gets 403 (a member always sees only their own).
Calendar year filter (2000–2100). Optional — defaults to the current year when month is given.
Month 1–12. Optional; on its own it means that month of the current year.

request.description:
Attendance history, newest first — clock-ins, clock-outs and pings.

The super admin sees the whole business and can filter to one member with userId; a member is always scoped to their own entries.

Period filter: year (+ optional month). month ALONE means that month of the CURRENT year — year is only needed to look at a past one. Omit both for the full history.

Each entry carries userActive: false once the member has been removed from the business (their entries stay in the history so it stays complete).

Paginated: optional page (default 1) + size (default 50, max 200); response carries count, page, totalPages, total.

item.description: Employee daily presence (attendance). Members clock in/out with a GPS location (which pushes a notification to the super admin); the super admin pings the team for a spot-check and reviews the history by member and month.

request.description: Returns the user's app settings (monitored apps + notification keyword filters). When nothing has been synced yet, returns defaults: empty monitoredApps/keyword lists, blacklistEnabled=true, whitelistEnabled=false.

Replaces the monitored-apps map (packageName -> issuer). Sending an empty object clears the list. Package names must match [A-Za-z0-9_.]+; issuers are trimmed and lowercased. Returns the full updated settings. NOTE: super admin only — a plain member gets 403.

Updates the notification keyword filters. Partial update: omit a field (null) to leave it unchanged; send an empty list to clear it. Keywords are trimmed, lowercased, and deduplicated. Returns the full updated settings. NOTE: super admin only — a plain member gets 403.
Toggles whether the QRIS image is composed onto the profile picture (default false). Returns the full updated settings. NOTE: super admin only — a plain member gets 403.
Toggles whether inventory management is enabled (default false). Returns the full updated settings. NOTE: super admin only — a plain member gets 403.

Toggles whether the business wants to receive voice ads (default false / opt-in). Bundled into the login + /me app-settings. Returns the full updated settings. NOTE: super admin only — a plain member gets 403.

Returns the QRIS image as base64 and business info for the authenticated user.

Response includes: type (MANAGED or UPLOADED), image (base64-encoded PNG), businessName, businessAddress, nmid.

If no image has been generated yet, one is created and stored on the first call.

type=MANAGED means the Bejo-generated QRIS. type=UPLOADED means the user has uploaded their own QRIS image which takes precedence.

Uploads a custom QRIS image. After uploading, GET /api/qris returns this image with type=UPLOADED.

The generated QRIS is preserved and can be restored with Reset QRIS.

qrisImage must be a valid base64-encoded string. NOTE: super admin only — a plain member gets 403.

Clears the uploaded QRIS image and reverts to the Bejo-generated one (type=MANAGED).

No request body needed. NOTE: super admin only — a plain member gets 403.

Inbound QRIS payment callback (SNAP-like QR MPM notify) from the QRIS merchant service (e.g. AstraPay). Server-to-server — no X-API-TOKEN and no JWT.

PoC mode (provider payload is buggy): every callback records a MANAGED transaction against the SEED USER'S BUSINESS (app.callback.default-username → its business_id) and pushes to EVERY device of EVERY user in that business. No NMID routing, no dedupe (each callback = a new transaction). X-TIMESTAMP is currently ignored (transaction date = now()). Raw payload stored in additional_info.

Returns HTTP 200 with the acknowledgment shape { id, billNumber, referenceNumber, amount, tip, status, createdAt } — NOT the standard envelope.

item.name: Ads
item.description:
Voice-ad campaigns: a ≤10s / ≤2MB voice clip pushed to one device, tracked through its lifecycle (CREATED → PREPARING → READY → STARTING → PLAYED → FINISHED, plus ERROR).

ADMIN requests (Create/Prepare/Play/List/Get) use X-ADS-ADMIN-TOKEN ({{adsAdminToken}}) instead of a JWT. DEVICE reports (Downloaded/Played/Location) use the target device's JWT ({{token}}).

Create saves adCampaignId + adDeliveryId to the environment for the other requests.

request.description: Create a campaign + upload audio (base64). Audio must be ≤2MB and ≤10s (validated before upload) and a real audio file — the embedded sample is a 1s silent WAV. targetUsername/targetDeviceId must be an active user with a logged-in device (session). Requires X-ADS-ADMIN-TOKEN. 201 with the campaign (state CREATED). Saves adCampaignId + adDeliveryId.
Push a PREPARE (data-only, with a 24h signed download URL) to the target device; state → PREPARING. The app downloads the audio and reports back.
Requires state READY (the app confirmed a good download). Pushes a PLAY; state → STARTING.
Paginated list of campaigns with their delivery state (newest first).
One campaign with its delivery/deliveries.

The app reports the download. success=true with a matching sha256+sizeBytes → state READY; a mismatch, or success=false (+ optional "error"), → state ERROR. Idempotent. Uses the target device's JWT; a non-target device gets 403.
The app played the ad. playedAt is WIB wall-clock (no timezone). With latitude+longitude → state FINISHED; omit them (background play) → state PLAYED, then send the location below.
Deferred play location (foreground-only), when the Played report couldn't include it. Both required; state PLAYED → FINISHED.
Health check — no X-API-TOKEN or JWT required.
